fix.notes: Only `is` and `not` keys tokenize with `>` as a separate operator; `has>value` is lexed as a single string and falls through to a name-text search, so it was never broken in the same way. The fix is confined to two guard checks in parse_criterion.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

Searches like `is>commander` were silently succeeding — `parse_criterion` in `find/search.py` passed the term straight to `is_subquery()` without checking the operator. Because `is_subquery('commander')` returns a valid SQL subquery, the search returned all commander-legal cards instead of raising an error.

## What changed

- `find/search.py` (`parse_criterion`): added an operator check before calling `is_subquery` for both the `is`/`has` branch and the `not` branch. Any operator other than `:` now raises `InvalidSearchException`.
- `find/find_test.py`: added `test_is_requires_colon_operator` covering `is>commander`, `is>=commander`, `is<commander`, and `not>commander`.

Note: `has>vanilla` tokenizes as a single text token (not a key/operator/term triplet), so it never reached this code path and was not included in the test.

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed (all checks passed)
- `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit find` — 61 passed, 48 deselected

Fixes #11215
fix.pr_title: Raise error for non-colon operators with `is:`/`has:`/`not:` (#11215)
